title: Ring Tilting (Sinj Alka)
summary: A rider at full gallop carries a long lance and tries to pass its tip through a small iron ring hung high on a cord above the track. The ring swings, the pace is fast, and only a steady hand and good timing take the centre.
howToPlay: Press and hold: a crosshair marks where the lance tip will be, and it shakes with the pace of the run.
Release when the crosshair sits inside the swinging ring; the lance needs a moment to arrive, so aim a little ahead of the swing.
Three runs make a round, and there are three rounds.
rules: Through the centre of the ring scores 3, the upper band 2 and the outer band 1; a miss scores nothing.
The ring swings from side to side and slightly up and down, so time your release.
Each run has a single try; your total over all runs decides the stars.
heritageNote: Held every summer in the Dalmatian town of Sinj since the early eighteenth century, the Alka is a riders' contest in which each competitor gallops the length of a street and aims a lance at a small iron ring hung above it. Riders from the surrounding Cetina region keep the contest alive in historic dress.
